audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's final response and narrative ending: Job's humbled reply, hearing/seeing shift, contested 'repent' phrasing rendered as retract/relent in dust and ashes, divine rebuke of friends for not speaking rightly, Job's intercession, restoration, daughters named, and Job's death full of days.

verses.restored: Job answered the Eternal and said:

familiar.text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

modern.text: Then Job replied to the LORD:

verses.restored: I know that you can do all things, and no purpose of yours can be cut off.

familiar.text: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.

modern.text: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.

original.text: ידעת כִּי כֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וְלֹא יִבָּצֵ֖ר מִמְּךָ֣ מְזִמָּֽה

verses.restored: Who is this hiding counsel without knowledge? Therefore I declared what I did not understand, wonders too wonderful for me, which I did not know.

familiar.text: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

modern.text: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.

original.text: מִ֤י זֶ֨ה מַעְלִ֥ים עֵצָ֗ה בְּֽלִ֫י דָ֥עַת לָכֵ֣ן הִ֭גַּדְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין נִפְלָא֥וֹת מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְלֹ֣א אֵדָֽע

verses.restored: Hear, please, and I will speak; I will ask you, and you make it known to me.

familiar.text: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

modern.text: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’

original.text: שְֽׁמַֽע נָ֭א וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי

verses.restored: By the hearing of the ear I had heard of you, but now my eye sees you.

familiar.text: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.

modern.text: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.

original.text: לְשֵֽׁמַע אֹ֥זֶן שְׁמַעְתִּ֑יךָ וְ֝עַתָּ֗ה עֵינִ֥י רָאָֽתְךָ

verses.restored: Therefore I retract/relent, and I am comforted upon dust and ashes.

familiar.text: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.

modern.text: Therefore I retract my words, and I repent in dust and ashes.” The LORD Rebukes Job’s Friends

original.text: עַל כֵּ֭ן אֶמְאַ֣ס וְנִחַ֑מְתִּי עַל עָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר

verses.restored: After the Eternal had spoken these words to Job, the Eternal said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My anger burns against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken rightly of me as my servant Job has.

familiar.text: And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.

modern.text: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל אִיּ֑וֹב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל אֱלִיפַ֣ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֗י חָרָ֨ה אַפִּ֤י בְךָ֙ וּבִשְׁנֵ֣י רֵעֶ֔יךָ כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב

verses.restored: Now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. Job my servant will pray for you, for I will lift up his face, lest I deal with you according to your folly, because you have not spoken rightly of me as my servant Job has.

familiar.text: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.

modern.text: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה קְחֽוּ לָכֶ֣ם שִׁבְעָֽה פָרִים֩ וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֵילִ֜ים וּלְכ֣וּ אֶל עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֤ם עוֹלָה֙ בַּֽעַדְכֶ֔ם וְאִיּ֣וֹב עַבְדִּ֔י יִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֧י אִם פָּנָ֣יו אֶשָּׂ֗א לְבִלְתִּ֞י עֲשׂ֤וֹת עִמָּכֶם֙ נְבָלָ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב

verses.restored: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Eternal had spoken to them, and the Eternal lifted up Job's face.

familiar.text: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.

modern.text: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s request. The LORD Blesses Job

original.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ אֱלִיפַ֨ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֜י וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י צֹפַר֙ הַנַּ֣עֲמָתִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה אֶת פְּנֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב

verses.restored: The Eternal turned the captivity/fortune of Job when he prayed for his friends, and the Eternal gave Job twice as much as he had before.

familiar.text: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

modern.text: After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.

original.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת שבית אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַ֧יֹּסֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה

verses.restored: All his brothers, all his sisters, and all who had known him before came to him. They ate bread with him in his house, showed sympathy, and comforted him for all the harm the Eternal had brought upon him. Each gave him one piece of silver and one gold ring.

familiar.text: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.

modern.text: All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל אֶחָ֨יו וְכָל אחיתיו וְכָל יֹדְעָ֣יו לְפָנִ֗ים וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ עִמּ֣וֹ לֶחֶם֮ בְּבֵיתוֹ֒ וַיָּנֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ וַיְנַחֲמ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עַ֚ל כָּל הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר הֵבִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיִּתְּנוּ ל֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ קְשִׂיטָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאִ֕ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם זָהָ֖ב אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: The Eternal blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys.

familiar.text: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

modern.text: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

original.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה בֵּרַ֛ךְ אֶת אַחֲרִ֥ית אִיּ֖וֹב מֵרֵאשִׁת֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי ל֡וֹ אַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר אֶ֜לֶף צֹ֗אן וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ גְּמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶֽלֶף צֶ֥מֶד בָּקָ֖ר וְאֶ֥לֶף אֲתוֹנֽוֹת

verses.restored: He also had seven sons and three daughters.

familiar.text: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

modern.text: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי ל֛וֹ שִׁבְעָ֥נָה בָנִ֖ים וְשָׁל֥וֹשׁ בָּנֽוֹת

verses.restored: He called the name of the first Jemimah, the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-happuch.

familiar.text: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Kerenhappuch.

modern.text: He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם הָֽאַחַת֙ יְמִימָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית קְצִיעָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית קֶ֥רֶן הַפּֽוּךְ

verses.restored: In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them inheritance among their brothers.

familiar.text: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

modern.text: No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.

original.text: וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א נָשִׁ֥ים יָפ֛וֹת כִּבְנ֥וֹת אִיּ֖וֹב בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם אֲבִיהֶ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: After this Job lived one hundred forty years and saw his sons and his sons' sons, four generations.

familiar.text: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, even four generations.

modern.text: After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.

original.text: וַיְחִ֤י אִיּוֹב֙ אַֽחֲרֵי זֹ֔את מֵאָ֥ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וירא אֶת בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת בְּנֵ֣י בָנָ֔יו אַרְבָּעָ֖ה דֹּרֽוֹת

verses.restored: Job died old and full of days.

familiar.text: So Job died, being old and full of days.

modern.text: And so Job died, old and full of years.
